tables.title: Table 3: Variations on the Transformer architecture. Unlisted values are identical to those of the base model. All metrics are on the English-to-German translation development set, newstest2013. Listed perplexities are per-wordpiece, according to our byte-pair encoding, and should not be compared to per-word perplexities.
notes: Unlisted values are identical to those of the base model.
All metrics are on the English-to-German translation development set, newstest2013.
Listed perplexities are per-wordpiece, according to our byte-pair encoding, and should not be compared to per-word perplexities.
In rows (A), varying number of attention heads and attention key/value dimensions, keeping amount of computation constant.
In row (E), positional embedding instead of sinusoids.

observations: The table includes multiple variants labeled (A) through (E) and 'big', with detailed hyperparameter variations.
Rows (A) have varying h, d_k, d_v while d_ff changes accordingly; other parameters inherit from base unless listed.
Rows (C) include multiple configurations with different N, d_k, d_v, and d_model values; some rows list only partial parameters.
Row (E) explicitly notes 'positional embedding instead of sinusoids' in the label column.
The 'big' model uses 300K training steps and achieves best PPL (4.33) and BLEU (26.4) among all listed rows.
Values for columns like d_k, d_v, d_ff, h are sometimes omitted in rows where they match base or are implied by context, but only explicit values are transcribed.
uncertainties: For rows where a parameter is omitted (e.g., d_k in row C_5), it is unclear whether it inherits from base or is intentionally unspecified; per instructions, we do not infer missing values.
In row (A) with h=1, d_ff=1 appears inconsistent with typical Transformer design (d_ff usually >> d_model), but transcribed as written.
Row (C)_6 lists d_model implicitly via d_ff=1024 but does not state d_model; per instruction, we retain only explicit values — d_model remains null.
The note says 'unlisted values are identical to those of the base model', but per instruction, we do not fill missing cells in 'values'; only explicit entries are included.
Column 'params ×10^6' has many nulls; no inference is made even if parameters could be computed from others.
